text:
Nate: PSA  woke up to the apartment smelling like hot plastic. space heater had shifted and tripped the breaker, which also killed my wall outlet where the router lives. whole-home wifi toast for a bit.
Elena: yikes, are you ok??
Nate: all good, just scary. unplugged heater and moved it away from the desk. breaker popped in the hall, flipped it back and modem/router came up but one of the switch ports is dead.
Priya: glad you're safe. breakers pop when there's overload or a short. if the port died after the event try a different patch cable and avoid the outlet until the heater area is cleaned.
Ollie: quick test: `ethtool eth0` or `ip link` to see link. sometimes the switch recovers after a reboot.
Nate: tried reseating cables and rebooting the switch. one port still shows no carrier. swapped to a spare PoE-less switch and ok now. posted pic of charred power strip: /files/IMG_burnt_strip.jpg :fire:
Darren: wow. please don't plug that strip back in. file an expense for replacement and maybe a small surge-protected UPS for router/modem.
Priya: agree, safety first. also wash hands if you touched melted plastic.
Nate: status-bot: reported and uploaded receipt request.
status-bot: Incident logged: HOME-2218. Reminder: submit home-office safety expense for damaged power strip under "Home office equipment" within 14 days.
Elena: pro tip: put heater on a separate circuit if possible, or at least not the same outlet as networking gear. heavy loads + cheap strips = bad times.
Ollie: if you plan to use a heater near your desk, get a grounded wall plug in a different circuit or use a small ceramic heater with tip-over and overheat protection.
Darren: also a tiny UPS (500-1000VA) for modem+router prevents abrupt drops during resets. hands-on: unlatch the old strip and dispose of it safely.
Nate: ordering a surge UPS and a metal-cased switch now. thanks for offers of spare gear  appreciate it. will keep invites audio-only if the network hiccups in the afternoon.
Priya: glad it was minor. reminder: if you need help installing a dedicated outlet or anchor points for the heater, facilities can help for approved home office setups.
Nate: noted. Cat is very unconcerned and is now sitting on the cold spot of the desk like a tiny judge. will post calmer desk pic after replacements arrive. :cat: :raised_hands:
